text:
lena: Quick sync — I'm proposing we stop using the global feature-flags SSM param and instead generate a per-model ConfigMap (managed by TF) that lives next to the Deployment so teams can roll model-specific toggles independently. Thoughts?

chris: I think per-model CM makes sense for isolation. main thing is making sure pods pick up changes — we should add a checksum annotation on the Deployment.

chris: example:
text_continued:
```yaml
# k8s/overlays/prod/deployment.yaml
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        configmap.reloaded.hash: "{{ checksum of configmap }}"
```

chris: TF can compute the checksum with the kubernetes_config_map data and set it in the deployment resource. :+1:

devin: For secrets we should NOT put them in ConfigMaps. Keep secrets in KMS-backed K8s Secret or Vault. If the flag is sensitive, keep a reference. If it's not sensitive then CM is fine.

maya: Another option is using a sidecar reloader (e.g., stakater/Reloader) or use file-based projected volume and inotify in the app. But checksum approach is simpler and doesn't need extra controllers.

jorge: Two operational Qs: 1) will TF manage both the ConfigMap and Deployment in the same module? 2) how does this affect helm releases we have for some models?

lena: Good Qs. Plan is: terraform module per-model that declares the configmap + updates deployment annotation. For helm-managed models we add a small tf resource that patches the deployment annotation (kubectl provider / kubernetes_manifest) so we don't change helm chart values except for models we fully manage.

amanda: Heads-up: I opened a draft PR with the TF module and a script to calc checksum (sha256 of yaml). PTAL: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/1123 :eyes:

config-bot: TF plan for pr/1123: https://ci.internal/infra/plans/98765 — shows changes to 8 resources (3 configmaps, 4 deployments, 1 role).

devin: Caveat: rolling deployments will restart pods even if the only change is the annotation — that is desired for flag propagation, but ensure we don't risk thundering herd for hot models. Suggest staggered maxUnavailable and scaled bursts.

chris: For hot models we can use canary label + rollout strategy: set maxSurge: 1, maxUnavailable: 0 and ramp traffic via routing layer. Also we should add a migration playbook for changelog of flags.

lena: Can someone from runtime review the patch for the k8s provider usage and verify the checksum expression? @chris @maya

chris: I'll take a look today.

maya: I can check helms and reloader implications tomorrow morning.

amanda: Also pinging @jorge for infra test coverage — please add an e2e that updates a configmap and asserts pods pick up new value within X minutes.

jorge: Will do. I'll add a small harness in k8s-test that flips a test flag and confirms via metrics + logs.

lena: TL;DR: moving non-sensitive per-model flags to TF-managed ConfigMaps, annotate deploys with checksum, keep secrets separate, add e2e and rollout guidance. I'll merge the draft once chris/maya sign off. Thanks. :tada:
